To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) accuracy in diagnosing cases of nonspecific complaints is higher than chance performance, 2) diagnostic performance is more accurate for physicians with more years of practice, 3) accuracy is higher for internists and emergency physicians than for family physicians, 4) accuracy is higher when the correct diagnoses are more prevalent, 5) accuracy is higher in cases with more substitutable cues, and 6) accuracy is lower when there is more consensus about cues.
